districts.label: SoMa
districts.oneLineDistinction: Converted buildings for office, creative and technical work
districts.shortDescription: SoMa offers San Francisco’s broadest central-city mix of offices, converted warehouses, studios and hybrid commercial buildings. Flex users may consider it when office, creative, technical and limited production needs overlap. The range is a strength, but also a warning: one block may offer polished office space while another contains older operational stock, so the exact subarea and property format must lead the comparison.
worthKnowing: Confirm loading, permitted use, building systems and customer-facing needs at the property.

districts.label: Dogpatch
districts.oneLineDistinction: Small-scale maker, studio and office-production mix
districts.shortDescription: Dogpatch supports a fine-grained mix of workshops, studios, small production buildings and office-like spaces within a historic mixed neighborhood. It can fit maker, design, technical or office-production users that do not need a conventional business park. The neighborhood scale and close residential adjacency distinguish it from Central Waterfront’s protected PDR core and SoMa’s broader commercial inventory.
worthKnowing: Verify noise, loading, ventilation, circulation and use compatibility for the address.

districts.label: Showplace Square
districts.oneLineDistinction: Showroom, design and production in warehouse buildings
districts.shortDescription: Showplace Square is a strong flex environment for users combining showroom, design, office, storage and light production functions. Former warehouse and industrial buildings support a distinctive cluster of furniture, interiors, contractors and creative businesses. Its trade and showroom orientation differs from Dogpatch’s neighborhood-scale maker fabric and SoMa’s office-heavy adaptive reuse.
worthKnowing: Confirm loading, public access, use approval and the balance of office versus production space.

districts.label: Central Waterfront
districts.oneLineDistinction: Production-led flex beside the protected PDR core
districts.shortDescription: Central Waterfront can support flex users whose mix leans toward fabrication, prototyping, assembly or production rather than conventional office. Its PDR core and mixed-use transition areas create different property contexts within the same broad geography. It is more operational than Mission Bay and generally less showroom-oriented than Showplace Square.
worthKnowing: Subarea, zoning, utilities, loading and environmental conditions require property-level review.

districts.label: Mission Bay
districts.oneLineDistinction: Research-oriented space in a newer institutional district
districts.shortDescription: Mission Bay matters to flex searches primarily where laboratory, research, technical and office functions overlap. The district’s newer projects and institutional setting differ from warehouse-derived flex in SoMa or Showplace Square. It should not be treated as generic flex inventory: specialized systems, use approvals and building formats determine whether a particular space can support technical work.
worthKnowing: Laboratory infrastructure, use, ventilation, power and buildout must be verified per property.
accessObservations: T Third light rail runs through Mission Bay along Third Street.

districts.label: Bayview Industrial
districts.oneLineDistinction: Operational flex for service, warehouse and production users
districts.shortDescription: Bayview can support flex requirements that remain operationally led, such as office paired with warehouse, service, production or fleet activity. The area’s practical industrial stock distinguishes it from polished office-flex or showroom environments. It is most useful when the business needs a real operating base and can investigate property-specific loading, circulation, utilities and compatibility.
worthKnowing: Do not assume office quality, loading, yard, power or circulation without property verification.
